about: The civilians of a crowded infiltration level, and when the player hides among them (T152). Each group is a flock (ai_steering's Flock, T150): too_close is the separation radius, sees_within the radius inside which a civilian counts the rest of its group, and weights are separation, alignment, cohesion, the group's wander target keeping clear of the other groups within strangers_within, and making way for the player and the guards, who do not steer round anyone, within make_way_within -- in that order; strongest is the largest force a civilian applies. A group walks its level's wander loop and turns to the next point once its middle is within next_point_within metres. Its top speed is the player's walk, read from rules.json, so a person can keep in step. The player is counted in a group when at least fewest of its civilians are within counts_within metres; walking upright, heading within in_step_degrees of the group's heading, blends in; sprinting, crouching, lying down, standing still or walking against the group stands out. In a group, a guard's percept is weighed by the reading, in one place: an eye that picks out the player multiplies its certainty by certainty_scale, and an ear that hears the player's footstep (covers_sounds) hears it as if its reach were footstep_scale of its own -- a footstep's 6 m becomes 1.5 m among the crowd's own steps; footstep_scale and certainty_scale were chosen by measuring the walk down the spine in crowd_test.gd. The reading also becomes the figure sign of intruder_network.json. match_within_seconds is how quickly alignment and cohesion answer (the flock's time to target), starting_pace the share of the walk a civilian starts at. Distances compare strictly: within means closer than. Every number is the kit's own, chosen by playing, not learned (invariant 6).
